title: According to Thy Gracious Word
description: According to Thy Gracious Word in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 139, “"In Remembrance of Me."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ac-cord-ing to thy gra-cious word, In meek hu-mil-i-ty, This will I do, my dy-ing Lord, I will re-mem-ber thee.

lines: This will I do, my dying Lord,
Thy body, broken for my sake,
My bread from heaven shall be;
When to the cross I turn mine eyes,
O Lamb of God, my sacrifice!
Remember thee, and all thy pains,
And all thy love to me;
Yea, while a breath, a pulse, remains,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
